sense.text: Additional notes on last week’s chapter. “And I saw a new heaven and a new earth: for the first heaven and the first earth were passed away”: based on the scriptures, there is just going to be a change of worlds; the earth abides for ever. “And there was no more sea”: the sea is the riotousness of the nations.

“And I John saw the holy city, new Jerusalem, coming down from God out of heaven, prepared as a bride adorned for her husband”: in 2 Esdras 9 the prophet Ezra saw a vision of a woman who transformed into new Jerusalem, and that is what this verse makes reference to. This city Jerusalem refers to the people, first and foremost.

precepts.why: “And Sion shall come, and shall be shewed to all men, being prepared and builded, like as thou sawest the hill graven without hands”: further proof that the city is the people. That goes back to Revelation 21:2.

sense.text: “And the foundations of the wall of the city were garnished with all manner of precious stones”: the same stones that were made for the ephod are the foundations of new Jerusalem. About four or five names seem somewhat different, due to translation from Hebrew into Greek, but it is all the same. We are surrounded by concrete today, and it cuts us off from our spiritual connection with the Most High. The foundations of new Jerusalem will have the elements, the minerals, that the ephod had, which allowed us to talk with the Most High. The Father and the Son will be the temple.

precepts.why: “And thou shalt make the breastplate of judgment.” “And thou shalt set in it settings of stones, even four rows of stones”: he explains how to set the stones of the ephod. “And the stones shall be with the names of the children of Israel, twelve, according to their names.” Notice what is similar between the ephod and Revelation 21.

“I pray thee, bring me hither the ephod”: David says I need that ephod, I have to ask a question. “And David enquired at the Lord, saying, Shall I pursue after this troop?” “And he answered him, Pursue”: David needed that ephod to speak directly with the Most High.

In the coming kingdom: “And it shall come to pass, that before they call, I will answer; and while they are yet speaking, I will hear.” The communication will be open for us with the Most High and his Son. You have a thought, and he already knows it.

sense.text: “And there shall in no wise enter into it any thing that defileth, neither whatsoever worketh abomination, or maketh a lie: but they which are written in the Lamb’s book of life”: for the Lamb’s book of life we had Revelation 3:5 and Daniel 12:1 last week. Some mistakenly believe other nations might be in the book of life.

precepts.why: An additional precept for the book of life: “To the general assembly and church of the firstborn, which are written in heaven.”

The firstborn first and foremost goes with Christ, but watch: “Israel is my son, even my firstborn.” The church of the firstborn is Israel, not Moab, not Edom, not Ham, not Ishmael. Only the Israelites.

“And death and hell were cast into the lake of fire”: death and hell refer to the grave and captivity, which will be done away with. “And whosoever was not found written in the book of life was cast into the lake of fire.” The other nations are not entering the coming kingdom after the thousand-year reign.

sense.text: “And he shewed me a pure river of water of life, clear as crystal, proceeding out of the throne of God and of the Lamb”: John is seeing a vision; it is written as a similitude, a metaphor, and we need the proper precepts to explain it. This is why the Old Testament is very important; the Christians who say don’t read it, it’s done away with, are agents of Satan. The water symbolizes the word of God. Do you see words coming in the air? No; it is a symbol.

“And on either side of the river, was there the tree of life, which bare twelve manner of fruits, and yielded her fruit every month”: understanding came out every month. “And the leaves of the tree were for the healing of the nations.”

precepts.why: The precept for the pure river: “And, behold, waters issued out from under the threshold of the house eastward.”
“That he might sanctify and cleanse it with the washing of water by the word”: when John and Ezekiel see water gushing out from the temple, it all symbolizes the word of God.

“But his delight is in the law of the Lord; and in his law doth he meditate day and night. And he shall be like a tree planted by the rivers of water, that bringeth forth his fruit in his season”: he brings forth understanding in his season. “His leaf also shall not wither”: his understanding shall not wither. This is why we must not walk in the counsel of the ungodly. All our judgments must be Bible based; videos and audios don’t persuade us, we go by scripture, like Matthew 18.

sense.text: “Behold, there ran out waters on the right side”: he is looking at a vision of the temple, and he sees waters gushing out from all sides of it.

“And when the man that had the line in his hand went forth eastward”: the line is a measuring instrument, and the man is an angel taking Ezekiel by the hand. “The waters were to the ankles”: Ezekiel 47 deals with time. When the truth first started to come out, the people’s understanding was only at the ankles. In the sixties the Israelites weren’t really keeping the Sabbath; they were still buying and selling and cooking on it, and the women dressed like women only on the Sabbath day.

“The waters were to the knees”: time has gone by, and the understanding of scripture has risen. “The waters were to the loins”: time has passed on and the waters have risen. Some camps never kept the new moon, or Tabernacles, until the Lord showed us in the law, and now people are mad because the Lord is using us.

“And it was a river that I could not pass over: for the waters were risen, waters to swim in”: the word of God covered the earth. It wasn’t at the ankles, the knees or the loins any more; it covered the entire globe.

“Then he brought me, and caused me to return to the brink of the river”: the angel brought him back to the bank to explain. “Behold, at the bank of the river were very many trees on the one side and on the other”: the trees in the garden in Genesis were people, and that is what this parable goes into. These trees are the man embedded in the word of God, Psalms 1:3.

“Which being brought forth into the sea, the waters shall be healed. And it shall come to pass, that every thing that liveth, which moveth, whithersoever the rivers shall come, shall live”: everywhere the word of God touches and they are obedient to it, they shall live. That is the leaves of the tree for the healing of the nations in Revelation 22.

“And it shall come to pass, that the fishers shall stand upon it”: in verse 7 we were trees, now we are fishers; Christ said I will make you fishers of men. “Their fish shall be according to their kinds”: we are not fishing for other nations. “As the fish of the great sea, exceeding many”: Israel cannot be measured nor numbered.

When black people go off into sin, remember Daniel in Susanna calling the wicked elders the seed of Canaan and not of Judah. Judge not according to the appearance, but judge righteous judgment.

“But the miry places thereof and the marishes thereof shall not be healed; they shall be given to salt”: every sacrifice is seasoned with salt. The miry places are this place, which will never be healed.

“And by the river upon the bank thereof, on this side and on that side, shall grow all trees for meat, whose leaf shall not fade, neither shall the fruit thereof be consumed”: the fruit is understanding. When the Passover, the feast of unleavened bread or the Sabbath comes, everybody must obey, and to obey means you will be healed in your land. Moab in their land must obey the commandments of God to be healed, and we will have officers set there to ensure everybody obeys.

It is twofold: it is talking about the actual fruit we will eat, but more so it goes into the word of the Most High. “And the leaf thereof for medicine”: the scriptures as well as the literal understanding of herbs.

Verse 13 down through chapter 48 is about the division of the land. Ezekiel was in the Babylonian captivity, under the Cushites. In the Persian and Median captivity the king of Persia let us go and build the temple again, as you read in Ezra, Nehemiah and Haggai. When we got back to the land we had to divide it according to the tribes of Israel and rebuild the temple according to Exodus and Numbers. That is what Ezekiel 47:13 through 48 is about, along with us sacrificing again.

precepts.why: “Open thou mine eyes, that I may behold wondrous things out of thy law”: this is why we ask the Lord to open our understanding when we pray.

Saying the same thing as David: “The eyes of your understanding being enlightened”: our spiritual eyes being opened. We are in darkness now, the season of night, and we ask the Lord to open our eyes so we can better guide the people, ourselves and our families.
The trees on the sides of the river: “And he shall be like a tree planted by the rivers of water, that bringeth forth his fruit in his season.”

The healing of the nations. “Every one that is left of all the nations which came against Jerusalem”: the nations not destroyed when Christ returns; there will be a lot of people left, to pay for their judgment and serve. “Shall even go up from year to year to worship the King, the Lord of hosts, and to keep the feast of tabernacles.” “Even upon them shall be no rain”: no rain means drought; the plants don’t grow, the cattle can’t eat, and you die. Everyone will celebrate God’s high holy days, or they will die.

“From one new moon to another, and from one sabbath to another, shall all flesh come to worship before me”: everybody on the planet will honour the Sabbath and the new moon. You won’t be celebrating Halloween or Kwanzaa ever again.
This whole chapter is a parable. “I am not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Israel.”

Christ’s parable of us as fishers: “The kingdom of heaven is like unto a net, that was cast into the sea, and gathered of every kind.” “And gathered the good into vessels, but cast the bad away”: this Bible is like a net. We go out and teach, and people come in. What if another nation comes in, or someone’s great-great-grandfather was an Edomite? “The angels shall come forth, and sever the wicked from among the just.” Don’t worry about it; the angels will separate them.

“From whence then hath it tares?”: some look like Israel but they are not; they are tares, the other nations. “Wilt thou then that we go and gather them up? But he said, Nay; lest while ye gather up the tares, ye root up also the wheat with them”: we could make a mistake through visuals and rip up an Israelite thinking he is another nation.

The miry places that shall not be healed. The feet and toes are the last kingdom on earth, America and the European Union. “The kingdom shall be divided; but there shall be in it of the strength of the iron”: the iron represents the military. “They shall mingle themselves with the seed of men”: the miry clay represents the mixed multitude of this kingdom. “And in the days of these kings shall the God of heaven set up a kingdom”: Israel United in Christ growing is the beginning of the kingdom. “And the kingdom shall not be left to other people”: the kingdom of heaven is not for other nations. “And the dream is certain”: it shall surely come to pass. This is the last empire on earth; we don’t have time for going off.

“For the controversy of Zion”: who the land of Israel belongs to and who the twelve tribes really are. “And the land thereof shall become burning pitch”: those are the miry places. “From generation to generation it shall lie waste”: there will be no healing for this place.

Officers set over the nations: “Because thou hast been faithful in a very little, have thou authority over ten cities.” The very little is the understanding we have today. New York alone is about eight million people, and to make them obey the word of God we need power. On the other side, over ten cities, you will have a regiment of men under you to make sure the dietary law and the dress code are obeyed. When the white man took over, he changed our language and made sure we never called ourselves Israelites again; when we are set over the cities, they won’t call themselves Chinese ever again. They go back to the God-given name: Moab.

“And every tree, in the which is the fruit of a tree yielding seed; to you it shall be for meat”: that was Adam’s diet, the diet of everybody on the planet before the flood, animals included. We won’t be eating chicken; on Passover we might have lamb or goat.

The knowledge of herbs. “For he hath given me certain knowledge of the things that are, namely, to know how the world was made, and the operation of the elements”: Solomon was on such a high level of understanding. “The beginning, ending, and midst of the times”: he saw the whole spectrum. “The alterations of the turning of the sun”: the Bible says the sun goes around the earth. “The natures of living creatures, and the furies of wild beasts”: Esau tags animals and puts cameras on them, but Solomon already knew. “And the reasonings of men”: he understood why you did the evil you did. “The diversities of plants and the virtues of roots”: we are going to get that understanding.

“And the gates of the city shall be after the names of the tribes of Israel.” “And one gate of Joseph, one gate of Benjamin, one gate of Dan”: the gate of Dan is not recorded in Revelation 7. That is why chapters 47 and 48 go into when we returned from the Persian captivity and had to divide the land.

sense.text: “Was there the tree of life”: the tree of life is symbolic of the Lord giving immortality to his people, the elect.

“And there shall be no more curse”: we are not going to be destroyed or go into captivity ever again. Israel shall be all righteous, so that curse will be done away with. “But the throne of God and of the Lamb shall be in it; and his servants shall serve him.”

precepts.why: “The knowledge of the commandments of the Lord is the doctrine of life: and they that do things that please him shall receive the fruit of the tree of immortality.”
What the curse is: “Cursed be he that confirmeth not all the words of this law to do them.”

sense.text: “And they shall see his face”: we will see Christ face to face, so don’t let there ever be the slightest doubt in your mind. “And his name shall be in their foreheads”: in their minds, when we overcome and meet him face to face, with the pure language.
“And there shall be no night there; and they need no candle, neither light of the sun; for the Lord God giveth them light”: that goes with Isaiah 60:20. “And they shall reign for ever and ever.”

precepts.why: “For now we see through a glass, darkly”: the glass is the Bible. We read it like we have shades on; some things we see, some we don’t, until we read it again years later. That is Ezekiel 47: the understanding at the ankles, then the knees, then the loins, then covering the earth. “But then face to face”: the Lord will deal with us face to face. “Now I know in part; but then shall I know even as also I am known”: the Lord knows each one of us; even the hairs of our head are all numbered.

When we are delivered from Babylon and the lands we are scattered in: “And I will bring you into the wilderness of the people”: the same wilderness we were in with Moses. “And there will I plead with you face to face.”

“And they shall look upon me whom they have pierced”: we will literally see Christ, with that same body that was pierced. “And they shall mourn for him, as one mourneth for his only son”: we will feel like it was our only child that died.

“For my determination is to gather the nations.” “For then will I turn to the people a pure language, that they may all call upon the name of the Lord, to serve him with one consent”: for then, after he destroys the armies of the nations. That means right now everyone is not calling on the Lord with one consent. We are not arguing with other camps over how to pronounce the name; to prove the pronunciation you would have to go back in time and hear the Hebrew, so everything we have now is by faith. Keep the commandments.

Brothers who say we already have the name contradict scripture: “And I will write upon him the name of my God.” “And I will write upon him my new name”: Christ has a new name, and it won’t be in English. It will be the pure tongue the Lord sets up, not the confusion out here today.

The Hebrew was already changing in Christ’s day: “Eli, Eli, lama sabachthani? that is to say, My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me? Some of them that stood there, when they heard that, said, This man calleth for Elias.” Some of the people that heard the Hebrew mistook what he was saying, and that lets you know the language had changed somewhat.

“Thy sun shall no more go down; neither shall thy moon withdraw itself: for the Lord shall be thine everlasting light”: that is our understanding. We are not going to lose our understanding ever again.

sense.text: “These sayings are faithful and true”: the same as Daniel 2, where the dream is certain. The sayings of this book shall surely come to pass. “The things which must shortly be done”: that is why we are going through this now, so you understand what will happen soon.
“Blessed is he that keepeth the sayings of the prophecy of this book”: you follow the scriptures as they come out, and the Bible says you will be blessed.

precepts.why: For the many who say the Bible is not faithful and true, this is what you say to the scoffer: “Produce your cause, saith the Lord; bring forth your strong reasons.” “Let them bring them forth, and shew us what shall happen”: show us in ancient writings why we went into slavery on ships, what will happen to America, Syria, Egypt. Islam, Christianity, the Gilgamesh epic, the Quran, the books of Buddha and Krishna can’t do it; only the Bible can. “Let them shew the former things, what they be, that we may consider them, and know the latter end of them.” “Shew the things that are to come hereafter, that we may know that ye are gods”: some say the black man is God; then why did God go into slavery? “Behold, ye are of nothing, and your work of nought: an abomination is he that chooseth you”: anyone who chooses Islam or Christianity is an abomination.
Why you will be blessed if you keep the sayings of this book: “Here is the patience of the saints: here are they that keep the commandments of God, and the faith of Jesus.”

sense.text: “I fell down to worship before the feet of the angel”: “See thou do it not: for I am thy fellowservant, and of thy brethren the prophets”: that is a heavy saying, for another class. A hint: in the book of Tobit the angel told Tobit he was of the tribe of such and such, of his brethren; the angel didn’t lie, we just don’t understand yet. “And of them which keep the sayings of this book”: first and foremost the book of Revelation, but it includes the entire Bible.
“Seal not the sayings of the prophecy of this book: for the time is at hand”: don’t hide understanding.

precepts.why: “But thou, O Daniel, shut up the words, and seal the book, even to the time of the end”: the understanding of what the Bible is talking about would come at the time of the end. That is why men and women are waking up and know they are Israelites now: the seals are being taken off. We are in the time of the end.

sense.text: “He that is unjust, let him be unjust still”: the unjust falls amongst our people first and foremost; there will be some good and some bad. You decide you are unjust, then be unjust still. “And he which is filthy, let him be filthy still”: you want to be filthy, then stay filthy. “And he that is righteous, let him be righteous still”: I want the Lord to see me and you as righteous. There is such a thing as repentance: David repented, Solomon repented. “And he that is holy, let him be holy still.”

precepts.why: “An unjust man is an abomination to the just: and he that is upright in the way is abomination to the wicked”: this is why the wicked despise Israel United in Christ and try to bring us down any chance they get.

“How much more abominable and filthy is man, which drinketh iniquity like water?”: sin is sweet to them; they have no scruples about anything wicked. When sin doesn’t bother you, when deceit comes out of your mouth and it feels normal, something is wrong. Pray to the Lord to change your spirit.

“Hearken unto me, ye that know righteousness, the people in whose heart is my law”: that is how you know you are on the right path. If the law is in your heart you have boundaries. “Fear ye not the reproach of men, neither be ye afraid of their revilings”: this is why we don’t fear the videos coming out against us.
He that is holy: “Wherefore the law is holy, and the commandment holy, and just, and good.” To be holy and righteous we must keep God’s law; that is Revelation 14:12.

sense.text: “And my reward is with me, to give every man according as his work shall be”: this goes with Luke 19, be thou over ten cities, over five cities. These are the rewards according to our works.
“I am Alpha and Omega, the beginning and the end, the first and the last”: we went over this last week, but some got confused. Christ is the first and the last.

precepts.why: “And he that overcometh, and keepeth my works unto the end”: until we die. “To him will I give power over the nations”: I want that reward. “And he shall rule them with a rod of iron; as the vessels of a potter shall they be broken to shivers”: we are not going to have mercy on the other nations. When the white man conquered us, he broke us and changed our thinking; when we rule this earth, we will break these nations to the will of God. “Even as I received of my Father”: we will get the same blessing Christ received.
“For since by man came death, by man came also the resurrection of the dead. For as in Adam all die, even so in Christ shall all be made alive.”
The genealogy on Mary’s side, from her father Heli, Joseph’s father-in-law: “Which was the son of Adam, which was the son of God.”

“The first man Adam was made a living soul; the last Adam was made a quickening spirit”: quickening means converting, changing. “The first man is of the earth, earthy: the second man is the Lord from heaven.” Paul was very heavy in his understanding; we will go into this in greater detail in other classes. Some things we speak plain, some we don’t.

sense.text: “Blessed are they that do his commandments, that they may have right to the tree of life, and may enter in through the gates into the city”: I want to enter through the gates, whether I am dead in this life or alive and caught up. If I were another nation, I would pray to the Lord, just let me be a servant to your people Israel. This is why we do all this work: the reward of entering through the gates of the city.

“For without are dogs”: without means outside the gates of the city. “And sorcerers, and whoremongers, and murderers, and idolaters”: those who left and make video after video out of hatred for their brothers are murderers in the spiritual sense, and their covetousness is idolatry. “And whosoever loveth and maketh a lie”: some people love and make lies, and they made those videos to make lies; they edit them with jump cuts so it sounds like it flows.

precepts.why: In case you forgot about the tree of life: “The knowledge of the commandments of the Lord is the doctrine of life: and they that do things that please him shall receive the fruit of the tree of immortality.”
The gates we all want to go through: “And had twelve gates, and at the gates twelve angels, and names written thereon, which are the names of the twelve tribes of the children of Israel.”

These are not four-legged dogs; he is talking about the two-legged dogs. “Beware of dogs, beware of evil workers”: the Bible calls evil workers dogs. “Beware of the concision”: people that talk at the mouth and aren’t saying anything, like the scribes and Pharisees.

Sorcerers: the coconut under somebody’s bed, the tarot cards, the Ouija board. “That maketh his son or his daughter to pass through the fire”: that is abortion, killing your babies. “Or that useth divination”: rolling bones on the floor. “Or an observer of times”: the horoscope. “Or an enchanter”: casting spells on people. “Or a witch”: a female. “Or a charmer”: the lucky charm, the rabbit’s foot, the four-leaf clover. “Or a consulter with familiar spirits”: like the movie Ghost, your dead aunt has a message for you. “Or a wizard”: the male version. “Or a necromancer”: someone that talks with the dead, like the woman who raised up Samuel.

Even if you have never done those things: “For rebellion is as the sin of witchcraft”: if you are rebellious to the laws of God, you are like a witch or a wizard. “And stubbornness is as iniquity and idolatry”: stubborn to the laws of God, you are like an idol.

Whoremongers are promiscuous men: “All bread is sweet to a whoremonger, he will not leave off till he die”: all he cares about is sexual gratification. Sisters who leave their husbands to find another man end up with this man, who will leave them and the children. Be patient and abide in God’s commandments.

The woman: “Thus shall it go also with the wife that leaveth her husband, and bringeth in an heir by another. For first, she hath disobeyed the law of the most High; and secondly, she hath trespassed against her own husband; and thirdly, she hath played the whore in adultery, and brought children by another man.” “Her children shall not take root, and her branches shall bring forth no fruit”: in the past, nobody in the whole nation of Israel married a child born of adultery.

It was a shame, and we have to bring that shame back: “In her virginity, lest she should be defiled and gotten with child in her father’s house.” Today it is socially acceptable, with new titles like baby daddy.
Murderers in the spiritual context: “Whosoever hateth his brother is a murderer: and ye know that no murderer hath eternal life abiding in him.”

If you are in the midst of evil, these scriptures should shame you to repentance. “Whosoever is angry with his brother without a cause shall be in danger of the judgment”: when a man says I apologize, it is over; if you hold on to it, that is a grudge, and the sin is on you. “And whosoever shall say to his brother, Raca, shall be in danger of the council”: brothers or sisters constantly insulting one another. “But whosoever shall say, Thou fool, shall be in danger of hell fire”: they never repented, so they are going to die.

Idolaters. They all say they worship the God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, but you judge by actions; by him actions are weighed. If you worshipped him, you would apply Matthew 18 to a problem with your brother. “Mortify therefore your members which are upon the earth; fornication, uncleanness, inordinate affection, evil concupiscence, and covetousness, which is idolatry.”

What they were covetous for: “For the love of money is the root of all evil: which while some coveted after, they have erred from the faith, and pierced themselves through with many sorrows.” Covetousness is idolatry.
Whosoever loveth and maketh a lie: “He that worketh deceit shall not dwell within my house: he that telleth lies shall not tarry in my sight.” You are not entering the kingdom of heaven.

“If a man say, I love God, and hateth his brother, he is a liar: for he that loveth not his brother whom he hath seen, how can he love God whom he hath not seen?” Christ instructed us how to deal with one another; if you can’t do that, don’t say you love the Lord.

sense.text: “I Jesus have sent mine angel to testify unto you these things in the churches”: the seven churches scattered throughout Asia. “I am the root and the offspring of David”: that is saying something, for another day.

“And the Spirit and the bride say, Come”: Christ is the Spirit, and we are the bride. “And let him that is athirst come. And whosoever will, let him take the water of life freely”: you have to desire the water of life like a thirsty man or woman.

precepts.why: “Ho, every one that thirsteth, come ye to the waters”: everybody that is thirsty, come get your thirst quenched with the word of God. “And he that hath no money”: it doesn’t matter if you don’t have money, come learn this truth. “Yea, come, buy wine and milk without money and without price”: that is why we put this on YouTube and Facebook free.

We must be thirsty for understanding, for truth, for the coming kingdom: “Blessed are they which do hunger and thirst after righteousness.” When you lose that hunger and thirst, Satan has entered the building. Money is a necessity, but godliness with contentment is great gain; when you want more than contentment, you are no longer hungry for righteousness.

sense.text: “If any man shall add unto these things, God shall add unto him the plagues that are written in this book”: this is why we tell you to be mindful of the other books popping up, like Jasher and Enoch; they have been tampered with. Some say God had mercy on Esau and forgave him, which contradicts Hebrews 12, where there was no repentance for him. Stay away from those books.
“And if any man shall take away from the words of the book of this prophecy, God shall take away his part out of the book of life”: the white man took words out.

“Surely I come quickly. Amen. Even so, come, Lord Jesus.” You might not have gained all the understanding yet, but rehearse your notes and pray to the Lord to open your understanding, as James 1 says: if any lack wisdom, let him ask. You will catch on.
